topic: Paediatric buckle and forearm fracture management

audits.title: Improving Management of Paediatric Buckle Fracture in Orthopaedic Outpatients: A Completed Audit Loop.
audits.standard: NICE NG38: buckle fractures treated with non-rigid cast or splint without routine follow-up

cycle1.result: 59 fracture clinic visits; mean 1.9 visits per child

audits.intervention: Parents taught about fracture type and soft cast removal and offered no further visits; information leaflet designed with plaster technicians and nurses
audits.other_findings: Authors recommend implementing the guidance in A&E as well as fracture clinics.
audits.citation: Baig MN, Egan C. Improving Management of Paediatric Buckle Fracture in Orthopaedic Outpatients: A Completed Audit Loop. Cureus. 2017;9(11):e1829. doi:10.7759/cureus.1829. PMID: 29326858.

audits.title: Early Management of Paediatric Wrist and Forearm Fractures in a Busy District General Hospital Emergency Department: A Retrospective Cohort Comparison Study and Audit of BOAST Guidelines.
audits.standard: BOAST early management of distal forearm fractures in children (May 2021): early ED manipulation, neurovascular and consent documentation, orthogonal X-rays, fracture clinic within 7 days
audits.setting: Emergency department, district general hospital with paediatric orthopaedic services, Gloucestershire Royal Hospital

cycle1.result: 23/72 (31.94%) manipulated in ED; 11 of 23 ED manipulations failed.

audits.intervention: Local trust pathway in line with BOAST introduced from July 2021 (analgesia/sedation, location, manipulation and referral guidance) with staff education.

cycle2.result: 73/87 manipulated in ED (p<0.00001); 63 (86.31%) acceptable reduction, 10 (13.69%) failed. BOAST compliance: neurovascular documentation pre-manipulation 93.10% (81/87), before discharge 64.36% (56/87); consent documentation 73.56% (64/87); orthogonal X-rays 100% (87/87); fracture clinic within 7 days 49.42% (43/87), mean 8.25 days.

audits.other_findings: Reasons for not attempting ED manipulation (14 cases) were not documented; about 63 hours of theatre time saved. Protocol changed so off-ended fractures are manipulated under sedation.
audits.citation: Fink BE, Pinjala MT, Gomes KP, Mason WT. Early Management of Paediatric Wrist and Forearm Fractures in a Busy District General Hospital Emergency Department: A Retrospective Cohort Comparison Study and Audit of BOAST Guidelines. Cureus. 2023;15(7):e41325. doi:10.7759/cureus.41325. PMID: 37405130.

audits.title: Enhancing Patient Management and Financial Efficiency: Adherence to National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guidelines for Pediatric Distal Radius Buckle Fractures.
audits.standard: NICE guideline: manage paediatric distal radius buckle fractures with a soft cast and discharge directly from the ED
audits.setting: Hull University Teaching Hospitals; emergency department and fracture clinic

cycle1.result: 33/84 discharged at first visit; 69 had a single X-ray, 12 had two and 4 had three X-rays

audits.intervention: Results presented to the department and ED; parents educated on fracture type and cast removal with option to forgo clinic visits; safety brochures; email reminders to fracture clinic staff about NICE guidance

cycle2.result: 62/64 discharged directly from the ED (42 focal rigidity cast removed at home, 10 backslab, 10 crepe bandage); 2 returned to plaster room and 1 to fracture clinic

audits.other_findings: Extra visits, radiographs and cast changes in the first audit cost £18,078 over 6 months.
audits.citation: Zaib J, Ahmad J, Kumar K. Enhancing Patient Management and Financial Efficiency: Adherence to National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guidelines for Pediatric Distal Radius Buckle Fractures. Cureus. 2023;15(8):e44198. doi:10.7759/cureus.44198. PMID: 37767248.

audits.title: Clinical Audit of Manipulation of Paediatric Forearm Fractures in the Emergency Department at a District General Hospital: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.standard: BOAST and GIRFT recommendations that units have protocols for manipulation of paediatric forearm fractures under procedural analgesia in the ED, avoiding admission and general anaesthesia; local standard operating procedure
audits.setting: Poole Hospital, University Hospitals Dorset NHS Foundation Trust, district general hospital emergency department and trauma and orthopaedics

cycle1.result: Pre-implementation (n=11 suitable fractures): manipulation in ED 1 (9.1%); theatre required 4 (36.4%).

audits.intervention: New standard operating procedure and paediatric fracture manipulation pathway in the ED using intranasal fentanyl and Entonox, agreed with ED, orthopaedics, radiology and theatre managers; information leaflets planned after cycle 2.

cycle2.result: Third cycle (n=52): manipulation in ED 9 (17.3%); theatre required 1 (1.9%). All nine manipulable fractures were manipulated in the ED.

audits.other_findings: Second cycle (n=74): manipulation in ED 11 (14.9%), theatre required 21 (28.4%); 27% of manipulable fractures were manipulated in ED and none of these later needed theatre. All manipulations were done by the orthopaedic on-call team, none by ED; documentation and consent remained areas for improvement.
audits.citation: Nasim O, Norman R, Gangadharan R, Oo TP, Kalderon J, Alhamarsheh A, et al.. Clinical Audit of Manipulation of Paediatric Forearm Fractures in the Emergency Department at a District General Hospital: A Quality Improvement Project. Cureus. 2023;15(12):e51095. doi:10.7759/cureus.51095. PMID: 38274930.

audits.title: Improving Patient Care and Streamlining Follow-Up: Compliance With National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guidelines for Pediatric Distal Radius Buckle Fractures.
audits.standard: NICE guidance for children's distal radius buckle fractures: removable splint instead of full cast and no routine follow-up; no target stated
audits.setting: Queen's Hospital, Burton upon Trent; emergency department and fracture clinic

cycle1.result: ED: 0% splint (all back slab). Fracture clinic: 62 (95.4%) full cast, 3 (4.6%) splint. Discharged at first visit 5 (7.7%); second visit 56 (86.2%); third visit 4 (6.2%).

audits.intervention: New ED and fracture clinic pathway (splint or soft cast with information leaflet and no follow-up), posters in ED and fracture clinic, and email reminders to staff.

cycle2.result: ED: 17 (19.5%) splint, 70 (80.4%) back slab. Fracture clinic: 44 (50.6%) converted to splint and 2 remained in splint (53%), 41 (47.1%) cast. Discharged at first visit 39 (44.8%); second visit 48 (55.2%).

audits.other_findings: Discharge at first visit remained suboptimal. Some casts were used because of limited splint sizes, patient preference or lack of technicians at weekends.
audits.citation: Ali F, Elmubark M, Mussab RM, Mubark I, Jayakumar N, Ashwood N. Improving Patient Care and Streamlining Follow-Up: Compliance With National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guidelines for Pediatric Distal Radius Buckle Fractures. Cureus. 2024;16(11):e73624. doi:10.7759/cureus.73624. PMID: 39677174.

audits.title: The Children's Urgent Reduction of Forearm Fractures in the Emergency Department (CURFFED) project : a national prospective trainee-led collaborative audit of practice.
audits.standard: BOAST Early Management of the Paediatric Forearm Fracture (2021)
audits.setting: 53 UK NHS hospitals including 8 major trauma centres (national trainee-led collaborative, CURFFED)

cycle1.result: Mean overall BOAST compliance 63% (42.5% to 86.9%). Pain scores 83 (20%); regular analgesia 372 (87%); complete pre-manipulation NV assessment 214 (50%), post-manipulation 147 (35%); consent 163 (38%); analgesia and advice on discharge complete 95 (23%); consultant review within 48 h 328 (78%); clinic within 7 days 238 (59%). 423/577 (73%) manipulated first in ED.

audits.other_findings: Median time to first manipulation 2 h 43 min in ED versus 18 h 47 min in theatre. Only 9 of 53 sites supplied a local protocol and 8 a patient information leaflet.
audits.citation: Gourbault LJ, Whitham R, Womersley A, Jones E, Christie A, Duggleby L, et al.. The Children's Urgent Reduction of Forearm Fractures in the Emergency Department (CURFFED) project : a national prospective trainee-led collaborative audit of practice. Bone Jt Open. 2026;7(4):531-539. doi:10.1302/2633-1462.74.bjo-2025-0338.r1. PMID: 41962925.

audits.title: Optimising Management of Paediatric Distal Radius Torus Fractures: A Complete Two-Cycle Audit Assessing Compliance With National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guideline NG38.
audits.standard: NICE NG38: non-rigid immobilisation (removable splint or bandage) and discharge without routine follow-up for distal radius torus fractures; target 100%
audits.setting: District general hospital emergency department and associated nurse-led Minor Injury Unit, Mid and South Essex NHS Trust (Basildon)

cycle1.result: Compliance 97/174 (56%) at DGH and 0/48 (0%) at MIU, combined 97/222 (44%). Rigid immobilisation 77/174 (44%) DGH and 48/48 (100%) MIU. Fracture clinic follow-up 128/222 (58%).

audits.intervention: Educational posters in ED and MIU, NG38 emailed to all clinical staff, teaching sessions (two at DGH, one at MIU) and reinforcement at governance meetings (October 2023 to February 2024).

cycle2.result: Compliance 131/164 (80%) at DGH (p < 0.001) and 29/94 (31%) at MIU (p < 0.001), combined 160/258 (62%). Fracture clinic follow-up 98/258 (38%) (p < 0.001).

audits.other_findings: Rigid immobilisation persisted in 33/164 (20%) at DGH and 65/94 (69%) at MIU; splint stock at the MIU may have contributed. No balancing measures were collected.
audits.citation: Rajan P, Pammi S, Nutalapati V, El-Tawil Y, Balineni BK, Seferiadis I. Optimising Management of Paediatric Distal Radius Torus Fractures: A Complete Two-Cycle Audit Assessing Compliance With National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guideline NG38. Cureus. 2026;18(5):e109442. doi:10.7759/cureus.109442. PMID: 42333334.
